Save raw JSON evidence locally (no uploading/publishing/deploying/running) under a new `registry-evidence/` directory in the current working directory (/work/output/artifacts/skill-bpmn-registry-discovery). content_blocks.text: Registry pull succeeded. Now let's list the full catalog and inspect it to find agent/queue/connector types.

Good, this covers the agent wrapper filtered lookup. Now let's also do a queue search and a connector search for completeness, and get the detailed record for one documented type (e.g. `Orchestrator.StartAgentJob` and `Orchestrator.CreateQueueItem`).
Now let's get detailed registry records for representative documented wrapper types — one agent type, one queue type, and one connector type.
All commands succeeded and returned valid, non-failure JSON. Let's verify each file's content quickly to confirm they contain real registry records (not error envelopes), then finalize.

All three detailed records contain real, well-formed registry data (Result: Success, full templates with XmlTemplate, ContextFields, BindingInfo — no fabricated IDs, all placeholders remain `{id}`, `{name}`, etc.). Let's do a final listing and cleanup check.

All evidence collected successfully with the live `uip` CLI (no fallback needed — the registry synced fresh and every call returned real success payloads). Summary of `registry-evidence/`:

| File | Command | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `registry-list-all.json` | `uip maestro bpmn registry list --limit -1 --output json` | Full catalog: 30 extension types (`ExtensionTypes`), 27 `Connectors`, 138 `Processes` with `ProcessesByType` breakdown |
| `registry-search-agent.json` | `uip maestro bpmn registry search agent --output json` | Filtered lookup surfacing agent wrapper types: `Orchestrator.StartAgentJob`, `Intsvc.AsyncExecution`/`SyncAgentExecution`/`AsyncAgentExecution`, `Orchestrator.StartAgenticProcess`, etc. |
| `registry-search-queue.json` | `uip maestro bpmn registry search queue --output json` | Filtered lookup for queue wrapper types: `Orchestrator.CreateQueueItem`, `Orchestrator.CreateAndWaitForQueueItem` |
| `registry-search-connector.json` | `uip maestro bpmn registry search connector --output json` | Filtered lookup for connector wrapper types (Integration Service `Intsvc.*` activities/events) |
| `registry-get-Orchestrator.StartAgentJob.json` | `uip maestro bpmn registry get Orchestrator.StartAgentJob --output json` | Detailed record: BPMN placement, context fields, binding info, and full `xmlTemplate` for the agent wrapper |
| `registry-get-Orchestrator.CreateQueueItem.json` | `uip maestro bpmn registry get Orchestrator.CreateQueueItem --output json` | Detailed record for the queue wrapper (binding pattern `queue`, `queueName` binding info, template) |
| `registry-get-Intsvc.ActivityExecution.json` | `uip maestro bpmn registry get Intsvc.ActivityExecution --output json` | Detailed record for the generic connector-activity wrapper (connection/folderKey bindings, discovery notes, template) |

All 7 files are raw, unmodified `--output json` CLI output, all valid JSON, all `"Result": "Success"`. No connection IDs, folder keys, tenant URLs, connector keys, or release keys were invented — every identifier-like field in the templates is a placeholder (`{id}`, `{connectorKey}`, `{connectionBindingId}`, etc.) as returned by the registry itself. Nothing was uploaded, published, deployed, debugged, or run — this was pure discovery/evidence capture.
